clue.text: European landmark in Rome, dirt cheap to renovate

indicators.note: renovating something rebuilds it, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A property tip: a famous European building in Rome could be done up for very little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Rome' looks like where the landmark stands, but Rome is fodder; the Arc de Triomphe is in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arc de Triomphe is the famous triumphal arch in Paris, an example of a European landmark.

clue.text: Where rook may go, affecting everyone

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a chess rook moves in straight lines, traversing the chessboard
second meaning: applying universally to all

explanation.walkthrough: The rook in chess slides along ranks and files, so it can travel from one side of the playing surface to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a measure applied to all people or categories equally, such as a pay rise for every employee.

clue.text: Police beginning to enter wood

parts.note: cops is slang for police officers

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of enter

explanation.surface: Officers start to move in on a patch of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket of trees, a little wood.

clue.text: Key: use leverage in business

parts.note: the Enter key on a keyboard
to prise something open is to force it with a lever

explanation.surface: Advice for getting ahead in commerce: exploit your influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use leverage' reads as business jargon, but it means physically levering something open.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a company or commercial undertaking, a synonym for a business.

clue.text: English lamb finally entering ring — spring back?

indicators.note: letters entering something go inside it, so they sit within the outer word

parts.note: a ring is a round shape; it also opens up to hold the inner letters
E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of lamb

explanation.surface: A young sheep from England bounds into a ring and leaps back out.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebound is to bounce back after hitting something, a synonym for springing back.

clue.text: Acting as supreme leader in general

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: ruling over everybody
second meaning: taken as a whole, on the whole

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the answer into two words, as in a commander set above all.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means considering everything together, so it is a synonym for broadly or in general.

clue.text: Father — one after Oscar?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal word for dad
second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for P follows the one for O

explanation.walkthrough: Oscar looks like a man's name, perhaps a son, but it is the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa is a childish or old-fashioned word for a parent, and it is also the radio code word for P.

clue.text: Auntie and doctor not half wrong — child's right!

indicators.note: letters that have gone wrong are out of order and must be rearranged
not half means only half the word survives, so the rest is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut back to its first three letters

explanation.surface: A relative and a medic are told off by a youngster who insists on being schooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' tempts as the anagram signal, but here it is fodder, halved to DOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling is widely held to be an entitlement of every young person, so education is a child's right.

clue.text: Thug also battered Welshman in old Welsh county

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Morgan is a typically Welsh name

explanation.surface: A violent man also beat up someone from Wales in a former county there.
explanation.walkthrough: South Glamorgan was a Welsh county around Cardiff from 1974 to 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: South Glamorgan was one of the administrative counties of Wales, abolished in 1996, so it is an old one.

clue.text: Well-respected place besieged by a rebel, unfortunately

indicators.note: a place besieged is surrounded, so it sits inside the other letters
things that turn out unfortunately go awry, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: A respectable town is sadly under siege by an insurgent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun, a town under siege, but it is the verb meaning to put.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reputable has a good name and is held in high regard, so the word means well-respected.

clue.text: Best to dock heading to dwarf planet

indicators.note: to dock is to cut off a tail, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: plum means the best, as in a plum job
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is told the best plan is to put into port before setting off for a distant world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a harbour, but it means cutting a tail short.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto was reclassified in 2006 from a full planet to a dwarf planet.

clue.text: Very fine total

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of fabric, extremely thin and see-through
second meaning: complete, utter, as in pure folly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Very fine' reads as high praise, but it means thin, as with delicate stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer describes diaphanous cloth, and also means absolute or utter, as in a sheer waste of time.

clue.text: Stuck in rut, a habitual state

indicators.note: the answer is stuck inside the following words, lodged across their letters

parts.note: runs across the end of rut, the a, and the start of habitual

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a routine is in a settled habitual state of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a frame of mind, but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, in the American West.

clue.text: Sharp dessert

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sour or acid in taste
second meaning: a pastry case with a sweet filling

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a single description of a tangy pudding; they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart means acidic or sour, and a tart is also an open pastry pudding with fruit or jam.

clue.text: Menu set on end of bench covering item for dinner, perhaps

parts.note: a table is a list set out in rows, as a menu is
to clot is to set or thicken, as blood or cream does

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of bench

explanation.surface: A list of dishes is placed at one end of a seat, wrapped around something served at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablecloth is the linen spread over a dining table, an item laid for a meal such as dinner.

clue.text: Bureaucracy, having shifted communist to the right, came to a point

indicators.note: shifted means moved along, so one part of the word moves position
the moved part goes rightwards, to the far end of the word

parts.note: red tape is excessive official procedure
a red is a communist: this names the opening chunk of the first piece, the one that moves to the end

explanation.surface: Officialdom, having moved a Marxist to the right politically, reached a sharp conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the right' sounds political, but it means moving the chunk rightwards to the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows gradually to a tip, so it came to a point.

clue.text: Person with complaint, argument that's nothing special?

parts.note: plain means ordinary, nothing special
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A grumbler is having a row that is not worth noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in reverse order: the argument comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a legal complaint against someone in court.

clue.text: First stage involves a racket

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap something up inside, so the outer word holds the others

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a journey or race
taken as written
a din is a loud noise, a racket

explanation.surface: The opening phase of something involves a tennis bat or a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests a bat or a fraud; here it means noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading means in first place, ahead of everyone else, as the leading runner.

clue.text: Stir as sleep passes

indicators.note: to stir is to mix things about, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sleeper starts to move as the night's slumber goes by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time elapses when it goes by, so the verb is a synonym for passes.

clue.text: Lengthen period of confinement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pull out longer
second meaning: slang for a prison sentence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Period of confinement' could suggest childbirth, but the slang sense is a spell behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch is to extend, and a stretch is informal slang for a term served in prison.

clue.text: Italian dish not bad, regularly seen behind bar

indicators.note: seen behind means placed after, so that piece follows the other

parts.note: a pole is a long bar

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of not bad

explanation.surface: A restaurant review: this Italian food is decent, often spotted at the back of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is a northern Italian dish of boiled cornmeal, served soft or set and fried.

clue.text: Construct one lacking English used

parts.note: to put up a building is to construct it

indicators.note: a word lacking something has that part missing, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: An instruction to build a unit without anything English in it, using second-hand parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put-upon is exploited or taken advantage of, so they are being used.

clue.text: Sound of swine in fine houses

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it inside, so the outer word surrounds the other

parts.note: OK means fine, all right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pigs make their noise inside smart homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like a noun, fine homes, but it is the verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: An oink is the grunting noise a pig makes, and swine are pigs.

clue.text: Dress ripped at top initially, darn it

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each word, so the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone tears their frock at the neckline and mutters a mild curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Drat is a mild exclamation of annoyance, used just like darn it.

clue.text: Pair of Manx cats love tropical tree

indicators.note: a Manx cat is born without a tail, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: the first of the pair: a cat, cut to two letters
the second of the pair, also cut to two letters
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Two tailless cats from the Isle of Man adore a tree in the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manx cat, from the Isle of Man, has no tail, so each CAT loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao is the tropical tree whose seeds give cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Primate briefly places church above devil

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: An archbishop, in short, ranks the church above the devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop beside church and devil, but it is the ape. 'Briefly' marks a shortened word, chimpanzee.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimp is the short form of chimpanzee, an ape and so a primate.

clue.text: Old South American occupying most extreme parts of Colombia

parts.note: occupying a place means being in it

indicators.note: the most extreme parts of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Colombia

explanation.surface: A native South American living in the remotest regions of Colombia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the people of a pre-Columbian empire in the Andes, an ancient South American civilisation.

clue.text: In conference, check rule

indicators.note: in conference means in talks, so the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: During a meeting, someone verifies a regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like verify, but it is the restraining sense of a horse's rein.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a period of rule by a monarch, and to reign is to rule.

clue.text: Clue I get with no working out, making progress slowly and carefully

parts.note: a tip is a hint, a clue

indicators.note: working something out means solving or sorting it, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver admits getting a clue without any reasoning, edging forward cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' looks like the solver's reasoning; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on the toes is a way to move quietly and cautiously, so the word means advancing with care.

clue.text: Brief success, cook's brilliant moment?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short-lived triumph that is never repeated
second meaning, read literally: a sudden burst of light in a kitchen pan

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from old flintlock guns, where powder flared in the pan without firing; the question mark flags the kitchen reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone or something that succeeds once, spectacularly, and then fades away.
